coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across 7 primary graph rendering libraries (React Flow/xyflow, D3.js, Cytoscape.js, Sigma.js, vis.js, react-force-graph, Cosmograph) and 5 commercial competitors (Ogma, GoJS alternatives, yFiles, KeyLines, Linkurious). Coverage includes: official homepages + docs (T1), peer-reviewed academic papers on graph visualization (T0 Bioinformatics/CHI), G2/Capterra/TrustRadius reviews (T2), HCI research on cognitive load + interaction design (T0), performance benchmarks Canvas/WebGL/SVG (T1-T2), npm download trends + ecosystem metrics (T2), analyst reports Gartner/Forrester (T1-T2), comparison articles from practitioner authorities (Cambridge Intelligence, Memgraph, Linkurious, PkgPulse) (T2), and community resources (GitHub, Medium, DEV Community) (T3). Deduplication applied across library comparison articles (overlapping in Cambridge/Memgraph/PkgPulse/FirstAI). Notable gap: paywalled Gartner PDFs referenced but not fetched; community Discord/GitHub discussions indexed as reference-only. Trade-off analysis surfaced: ease-of-use (vis.js) vs performance (Sigma.js WebGL) vs customization (D3.js) vs workflow-authoring (React Flow). HCI pain points documented: hairballs/visual clutter, cognitive load on large graphs, slow layout computation.
